nodes.description: Gavin's seam 2026-09-13, and it is exact. AG-UI (ag-ui-protocol/ag-ui, 15.8k stars, MIT) is 'an open, lightweight, event-based protocol that standardizes how AI agents connect to user-facing applications' - roughly 16 event types, transport-agnostic across SSE, WebSockets and webhooks, with first-party integrations for Microsoft Agent Framework, Google ADK, AWS Strands, Mastra, Pydantic AI, Agno, LlamaIndex and AG2, partnerships with LangChain and CrewAI, and a COMMUNITY SDK for the Claude Agent SDK - the thing Gavin builds on. OpenUI (openui.com, thesysdev/openui, ~7k stars, Thesys Inc., open source) is the 'Open Standard for Generative UI' - agents 'stream live charts, forms, cards, tables, and dashboards faster, with fewer tokens' than JSON, renderer-agnostic across React, Vue, Svelte, React Native and email, with progressive rendering as the model responds. THE SEAM: they are complementary halves, and Gavin already built both by hand. AG-UI standardizes the WIRE - which is packages/griot-widget's drive() plus the brainstorm-channel meta contract on :52342 that gavel deliberately inherits ('do NOT rename'). OpenUI standardizes the PAYLOAD - which is griot-widget's render() plus frame-template.html and the fidelity engine. The broker's registry.cjs register(name, {render, drive, verbs}, {readiness}) is a hand-rolled version of exactly this pairing. Not a replacement: a named, specified, ecosystem-backed description of a shape he arrived at independently - which makes them pattern sources and, where useful, interop targets. Named, not built.

verification.evidence: Both fetched from source this session: ag-ui README (tagline, event model, transports, integration roster, MIT, 15.8k) and openui.com (tagline 'Open Standard for Generative UI', Thesys authorship, renderer targets, ~7k). nodes.title: worktrunk as the branch-state reference for a workgraph view in prism-cli
nodes.description: Gavin's seam, refined by him mid-thread to the right target: 'the prism cli could use this as a way to show workgraphs, or at least start the exploration in TUI.' HONEST CORRECTION FIRST: worktrunk (max-sixty/worktrunk, 5.6k stars, Rust, MIT OR Apache-2.0) is a CLI, not a TUI - its own README says 'a CLI for git worktree management, designed for running AI agents in parallel'. It has an interactive picker, not a terminal UI. It also has NO graph, no edges, no blockers and no lanes: it tracks branches and worktrees with status indicators, nothing more. So it is not our workgraph TUI. WHAT IT ACTUALLY OFFERS: the reference for branch-state-in-a-terminal, and a design principle worth lifting verbatim - 'Worktrees are addressed by branch name; paths are computed from a configurable template', which is what makes worktrees 'as easy as branches'. Its verb set (wt switch / list / merge / remove) plus hooks, LLM-generated commit messages and CI status display is a compact vocabulary for exactly the surface Prism needs. And it was built for running AI agents in PARALLEL, which is precisely what Gavin's headless claude.exe -p stage-walks do - today they run one at a time in one working tree. THE REAL SEAM, per N15: prism-cli is already a Bubbletea TUI and already parses 'git worktree list --porcelain' into WorktreeInfo - and knows nothing about the workgraph. Joining each WorktreeInfo to its workgraph node would turn a worktree list into a lane view carrying state, readiness and blocker counts. The vessel exists; the join does not. Named, not built.

verification.evidence: worktrunk README fetched from source: CLI not TUI, Rust 99.5%, MIT OR Apache-2.0, 5.6k stars, verbs wt switch/list/merge/remove, branch-name addressing with configurable path template, no dependency or graph modelling. prism-cli's Charm stack and Worktree* message types verified on disk (see N15).
verification.result: CONFIRMED - worktrunk is a pattern source, not the TUI; prism-cli is the vessel and is half-built.

nodes.note: GAVIN'S CORRECTION, recorded 2026-09-13 and it reframes this node: he uses TUI and CLI interchangeably ON PURPOSE, not loosely. His stated ideology - form and function feed each other, and a great deal of Prism came from building the TUI and thinking about how to REPRESENT THE SYSTEM in a CLI environment. The terminal constraint is a design forcing function, not a rendering detail: deciding what survives in a line of text is deciding what is essential. So the CLI-vs-TUI line drawn above is technically accurate and was rhetorically overweighted. THE DISTINCTION THAT ACTUALLY CARRIES WEIGHT for this seam is not whether worktrunk draws boxes - it is that worktrunk has NO EDGES. It models branches and worktrees with status indicators and nothing more: no dependencies, no blockers, no lanes, no graph. That is the real gap between it and a workgraph surface, and it holds whether the thing is a CLI or a TUI. Keep the verified fact (its README says CLI); stop treating it as the point.

closureModel.rule: Lane closure is COMPUTED, never judged: a node counts closed if its state is in closedStates, open if in openStates. Both lists live here so the percentage is always auditable and a new state cannot silently change a number without being classified first.

readinessModel.rule: Readiness is a QUICK-CLOSE aid, not a decision. Five factors, 0-20 each, summed to 0-100, each stored separately and each tagged measured or judged so the number always decomposes. The LOWEST factor names the reason the item is not closed - that is the whole point.

factors.tooling: exists and reachable 20 | exists unreachable 10-12 | must be built 0
factors.blastRadius: INVERTED - one file 20 | one repo 12-16 | multi-repo 8 | cross-surface 0-4
factors.decisionDebt: no ruling needed 20 | one ruling 10 | unresolved conflict 0

readinessModel.dispositionSource: prism-gavel's existing decision axis - reused, not reinvented (see N13).
readinessModel.closeSemantics: defer and pass clear the item from the live view; the node and its record stay. An S node left undisposed past its useful life IS drift by the Suite Drift Codex's own definition and should age into a griot-drift-log entry.
